newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt security yields seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt security yields seen stabilising.

text.p: Hungarian government security yields on the secondary market are seen halting, or at least slowing a two-week rising trend which reversed a decline of months, dealers said on Monday.
"As I feel, the market has stabilised," said Robert Schutz of Bank Austria Investment.
"I am not completely sure that the rising trend is over," said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities. "But I do not expect further substantial rises."

Government security yields have been increasing on the secondary market and at auctions since two weeks ago when the National Bank of Hungary raised its six-month deposit rate by 0.25 percent to 21.00 percent.
The move, which hit the markets as a surprise and cooled previous repo cut and interest rate decline expectations, was aimed at protecting savings.
Two- and five-year government bond yields on the secondary market rose by some 0.5 percent, while three-year bond yields went up by some 0.7 percent following the NBH rate hike, dealers said.
Reuters benchmark yields show that two-year bonds stand at 19.06 percent, three-year bonds at 17.78 percent, while five-year yields are at 16.18 percent.
Interest rates are seen dropping later this year, but they are unlikely to ease until the NBH keeps its repo and deposit rates at the current levels, dealers said.
Hungary expects average inflation to go down to some 17 percent this year from 23.6 percent in 1996.
Year-on-year inflation is running at 18.8 percent.
